claims.text: The governing measurement is the trace figure, not the rounded copy. The driver's own GPS polyline runs 10.13 km against a booked optimal of 7.4 km, an excess of 2.73 km — 36.89% of optimal. Both limb tests of POL-RD-01 pass: the excess is greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms and greater than 20% of optimal_distance_km, so the deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip's own trace.

No exculpatory clause reaches this detour. The only traffic advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-00534-01, is MISSING — the artifact carries no payload and weight 0.0, and its absence states that no advisory covers the optimal corridor in this window. POL-RD-03 cannot run, no shortest-lawful-alternative figure exists, and no closure-adjusted optimal can be substituted for the booked 7.4 km.

The detour was not rider-requested. The chat log for this trip carries a single message and it is from the driver — 'setting off now' — with waypoint_hint null. There is no rider instruction naming any place or road, so neither the source requirement nor the specificity requirement of POL-RD-04 is met, and there is no waypoint for the 200 m corroboration test to be run against.

The endpoints were never moved. The trip record shows pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at both null, and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min both null. POL-RD-05 has nothing to re-baseline, and no distance driven on this trip falls to be excluded as pre-amendment.

POL-RD-12 does not rescue the driver. It applies only where trip_record.vehicle_type is RYDE_POOL; this trip is RYDE_X, solo_optimal_distance_km is null, and no matched-itinerary optimal is recorded anywhere. There is therefore no pooled baseline to broaden, and the booked 7.4 km optimal remains the baseline for the POL-RD-01 test.

The driver's own statement concedes the extra stop — 'The second pickup was practically on the way' — and this trip was booked and billed on the RYDE_X product at solo price. Distance spent collecting that second passenger is not on the booked itinerary and no clause of this policy excludes it from excess; 'she got to her destination on time' and 'nobody was harmed' engage no clause at all and do not bear on the arithmetic.

The trace needs no independent corroboration because it is not impaired for policy purposes. It carries 163 fixes at a 10-second cadence, coverage 100%, zero gaps and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0 seconds, so none of POL-RD-07(a), (b) or (c) fires and the deviation may properly be established on the gps_trace alone.

The rider discharges the POL-RD-08 burden. trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip identifier TRP-00534 and align on the 17:00–17:06 pickup window, and the excess of 2.73 km clears both POL-RD-01 limbs. The rider profile shows deviation_claims_60d of 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated of 0, so the beyond-trace corroboration condition in that clause is not triggered and cannot be used to discount this claim.

The remedy is arithmetic under POL-RD-02 and it is a partial refund. The fare model on the breakdown is METERED and the surge multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier is 1.0, so recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 × 7.4 + 0.28 × 13.0) × 1.0 + 0.80 platform fee = 13.79. Charged_total is 19.74; the refund is 19.74 − 13.79 = 5.95, which is 30.1% of charged — above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and well below the 90% share that would convert it to a full refund.

No pass-through line adds to or is netted against that figure. The fare breakdown itemises no ERP gantry, no toll and no airport surcharge — all are zero — and the trip neither originates at an airport nor crosses a gantry, so POL-RD-09 yields no standalone correction and the refund stands at the 5.95 computed under POL-RD-02, with no line counted twice.

I do not press a full refund. POL-RD-06 is available only where the deviation is additionally MATERIAL — over 50% of optimal or over 8.0 km absolute — and this excess is 36.89% and 2.73 km, below both. In any event no repeat pattern exists: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 250 completed trips in 90 days. The correct outcome on this record is the PARTIAL_REFUND of 5.95 under POL-RD-02.

claims.text: The excess on this trip is established but it is not MATERIAL. The governing trace figure is 10.13 km against the booked optimal of 7.40 km, an excess of 2.73 km — 36.89% of optimal. POL-RD-01 makes a deviation material only when the excess exceeds 50% of optimal OR exceeds 8.0 km absolute; neither is met here. Because the deviation is not material, POL-RD-06's driver_profile check is not engaged, and no repeat-pattern uplift, no FULL_REFUND uplift and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral can follow from this trip.

Even if the driver_profile is consulted, no repeat deviation pattern is ESTABLISHED under POL-RD-06. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0, where the clause requires 3 or more; and deviation_flags_90d divided by completed_trips_90d (250) is 0.00, far below the 0.05 the clause requires. POL-RD-06 therefore yields nothing at all — not the balance-shift in limb (a), not the FULL_REFUND uplift in limb (b), and not the conduct referral in limb (c) — and POL-GEN-01 forbids substituting any other profile field (rating, account_age_days, lifetime_trips, prior_deviation_flags) for the two counters the clause actually names.

The ceiling on any refund is the POL-RD-02 arithmetic, and it is modest. charged_total is 19.74; the recomputed optimal-route fare is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 7.4 + 0.28 x 13.0) x the 1.0 surge multiplier recorded on the fare_breakdown) + 0.80 platform fee = 13.79; refund = 19.74 - 13.79 = 5.95, which is 30.1% of the charge. A FULL_REFUND requires the refund to be 90% or more of charged_total under POL-RD-02, or a MATERIAL deviation substantiated on this trip's own evidence together with an established POL-RD-06 pattern; neither is present. The rider's demand for the whole 19.74 is unsupported, and would in any event return the 3.80 base fare and 0.80 platform fee that no clause refunds and that POL-RD-02's recomputation deliberately retains.

Nothing is owed as a pass-through correction under POL-RD-09. The fare_breakdown itemises no ERP gantry lines (off-optimal-route ERP total 0.00, on-optimal-route total 0.00), no tolls, and no airport surcharge — and in any case a surcharge line would be improper here, since the trip neither originates nor terminates at an airport. There is accordingly no off-route or phantom line to refund standalone, and nothing may be added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure.

The driver has no exculpatory clause on this record, and I do not stretch for one. The only traffic advisory is absent: EV-ADVIS-00534-01 is MISSING, its status is MISSING with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight_multiplier 0.0, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run at all. The chat log EV-CHAT-00534 holds a single message, from the driver — 'setting off now' — with waypoint_hint null, so POL-RD-04's rider-instruction corroboration test is undecidable on the record rather than satisfied; the clause is simply unavailable, as it expressly provides where no waypoint and no named road exist. And no pickup or dropoff amendment is recorded (pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null), so POL-RD-05 does not apply. The excess therefore stands and the case is governed by the POL-RD-02 partial refund of 5.95.

ruling.explanation:
Both of you are broadly right about what happened, and the money follows arithmetic rather than blame.

ROUTE. The governing measurement is the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00534): it runs 10.13 km against the booked optimal of 7.40 km, an excess of 2.73 km, or 36.89% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 tests pass (more than 0.8 km absolute and more than 20% of optimal), so a route deviation is ESTABLISHED. It is NOT a material deviation: 36.89% is below the 50% mark and 2.73 km is below the 8.0 km mark, so the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is not engaged. In any event the driver's record shows no repeat pattern (deviation_flags_90d 0 against 250 completed trips in 90 days), so no full-refund uplift and no driver-conduct referral arise.

NO EXCULPATION. The only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-00534-01, is MISSING (status MISSING, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0); it carries no fact and its absence, not its content, is what is used, so it does not cap confidence. POL-RD-03 therefore cannot run and no closure-adjusted optimal can replace the booked 7.40 km. The chat log (EV-CHAT-00534) holds a single message, from the driver - 'setting off now' - with no waypoint, so POL-RD-04's rider-instruction test has nothing to run against. No pickup or dropoff amendment is recorded, so POL-RD-05 does not apply. The trip is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline does not apply and the booked 7.40 km stands.

THE SECOND PICKUP. The driver's statement that 'the second pickup was practically on the way' is accepted as an admission that the extra stop happened, and the rider's account of it is credited. But no clause of this policy excludes a non-rider-requested stop's distance from the excess, and this was not a pooled product, so it does not alter the arithmetic. 'She got to her destination on time' and 'nobody was harmed' engage no clause.

REMEDY (POL-RD-02). The fare model is METERED and the surge multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier is 1.0. recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 7.40 + 0.28 x 13.0) x 1.0 + 0.80 platform fee = 13.79. charged_total = 19.74. Refund = 19.74 - 13.79 = 5.95, which is 30.1% of the charge - above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and below the 90% that would convert it to a full refund. No ERP, toll or surcharge line exists to add under POL-RD-09 (all itemised totals are 0.00, and the trip neither originates nor terminates at an airport), so nothing is counted twice.

The rider's request for the whole 19.74 is not supported: the recomputation deliberately retains the base fare and platform fee, and no clause refunds them. The outcome is a PARTIAL REFUND of SGD 5.95; the rest of the charge stands. No clause produces a referral in this case.

POL-RD-12 does not apply: the product is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null, so the booked 7.40 km optimal remains the baseline.

ruling.explanation:
Rider — the outcome is a partial refund of SGD 5.95; your request for the full SGD 19.74 is not supported.

The deviation is established. The GPS trace EV-GPS-00534 runs 10.13 km against the booked optimal of 7.40 km, an excess of 2.73 km = 36.89% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 limbs pass (over 0.8 km and over 20%), so the deviation stands on this trip's own trace. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 163 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage and no gaps, so it carries the finding by itself and needs no independent corroboration. No exculpatory clause rescues the driver: the only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-00534-01, is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), so POL-RD-03 cannot be run; the chat log EV-CHAT-00534 holds a single message, the driver's 'setting off now', with waypoint_hint null, so POL-RD-04's rider-instruction test cannot be run and the clause is unavailable; and no pickup or dropoff amendment is recorded (both amendment timestamps and amended_optimal fields null), so POL-RD-05 has nothing to re-baseline. POL-RD-12 does not apply — this is a RYDE_X trip, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02 (fare model METERED; surge 1.0 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier): recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 × 7.40 + 0.28 × 13.0) × 1.0 + 0.80 = 13.79. Charged_total is 19.74, so the refund is 19.74 − 13.79 = 5.95 — above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and well below the 90% of charged that would convert it to a full refund. Your claim to the whole amount fails because the deviation is not MATERIAL: 36.89% is below the 50% figure and 2.73 km is below the 8.0 km figure, so POL-RD-06's full-refund uplift is not engaged; and in any event no repeat pattern is established (deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 250 completed trips in 90 days). POL-RD-02's recomputation deliberately retains the base fare and platform fee.

Driver — your account is accepted so far as it goes. Your statement that 'the second pickup was practically on the way' is an admission of the extra stop and is consistent with the trace, but it does not reduce the excess: distance spent collecting a second passenger is not on the booked RYDE_X itinerary and no clause of this policy excludes it. 'She got to her destination on time' and 'nobody was harmed' engage no clause. No pass-through correction arises under POL-RD-09 — the fare breakdown itemises no ERP gantry, no toll and no airport surcharge. No POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral issues, because no repeat deviation pattern is established. No disputed line lacks a counterpart, no timestamps conflict, and confidence sits above the floor, so nothing here escalates.

ruling.explanation:
This was a solo RYDE_X booking, not a shared ride, and the GPS record settles the route question. The trace is clean — 100% coverage, 163 fixes at a 10-second cadence, zero gaps and a 0-second maximum inter-fix gap — so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)–(c) and the deviation is measured straight from it. The governing figure is gps_trace.trace_distance_km = 10.13 km against the booked optimal_distance_km of 7.4 km, an excess of 2.73 km, or 36.89% of optimal. That clears both POL-RD-01 tests (over 0.8 km and over 20% of optimal), so a deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip's own trace alone.

No clause excuses the excess. The only chat message is the driver's "setting off now", sent by the driver with waypoint_hint null, so POL-RD-04's rider-instruction and 200 m corroboration tests cannot be met and the clause is simply unavailable. Neither endpoint was moved (pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null; amended_optimal_distance_km is null), so POL-RD-05 has nothing to re-baseline. The vehicle type is RYDE_X and solo_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-12's pooled-itinerary baseline does not apply and the booked 7.4 km stands. The fare is METERED, not an upfront quote, so POL-RD-11 does not run; and no closure is asserted by anyone, so the missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00534-01 (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) decides nothing here. Its absence is citable under POL-GEN-02, but the ruling does not rest on it and no POL-RD-03 exoneration was invoked. The driver's own statement that the second pickup was "practically on the way" confirms an extra stop, but on a solo RYDE_X product no clause excludes distance spent collecting a co-rider, so that distance stays in the excess.

The deviation is not MATERIAL — 36.89% is below 50% and 2.73 km is below 8.0 km absolute — so POL-RD-06's driver_profile check is not engaged. Even when consulted, driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 (the clause needs 3 or more) and 0 ÷ 250 completed trips is 0.00 (the clause needs 0.05 or more), so no balance-shift, no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral follows; the lifetime and reputation fields (prior_deviation_flags, rating, account_age_days, lifetime_trips) may not be substituted, per POL-GEN-01.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02, not discretionary. The fare breakdown is METERED with a surge multiplier of 1.0 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier: recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 × 7.4 + 0.28 × 13.0) × 1.0 + 0.80 platform fee = 13.79. Charged_total is 19.74, so the refund is 19.74 − 13.79 = 5.95, which is 30.1% of the charge — above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and well below the 90% share that would convert it to a full refund. The fare carries no ERP gantry lines, no tolls and no airport surcharge (all 0.00), so POL-RD-09 yields no standalone correction and nothing is counted twice. The rider's profile shows deviation_claims_60d of 0, so the beyond-trace corroboration condition in POL-RD-08 is not triggered.

To the rider: your point that you paid solo price on a trip that took in a second passenger is well taken on the facts, but the policy's remedy for an established deviation is the recomputed-fare arithmetic, which leaves the SGD 3.80 base fare and SGD 0.80 platform fee in place — the whole SGD 19.74 is not refundable. To the driver: an unexcused excess of 2.73 km cannot stand, but nothing here is treated as material, no repeat pattern is found and no conduct referral is recorded. Ruling: PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 5.95 to the rider. Confidence 0.9; the deciding facts (both distance figures and the refund arithmetic) are carried by artifacts at weight 1.0, so nothing drags the ruling below the 0.70 floor.
